page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 192 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This server configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a Passmark CPU score of 58,480.28 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,663.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. The hardware demonstrates high efficiency in specialized tasks, with strong results in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory performance is robust, showing top-tier uncached read and write bandwidths of 259.28 GB/sec and 114.19 GB/sec respectively. Additionally, the platform excels in static web serving throughput and prompt processing for small to medium language models.

From a resource density perspective, the n4-standard-48 offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for general-purpose workloads, avoiding the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all disk I/O relies on network-attached storage, which may limit performance for highly disk-intensive applications. This instance is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
